The cryptocurrency exchange CoinEx suffered a hacker attack. The cause of the incident was initially determined to be the leakage of hot wallet private keys. The damage caused is estimated to have reached US$70 million, and the impact has affected multiple blockchains. CoinEx tweeted that it had identified and quarantined suspicious wallet addresses related to the hack and that deposit and withdrawal services had been suspended. On September 13, SlowMist found during the analysis process that CoinEx hackers were related to Stake.com hackers and Alphapo hackers. CoinEx hackers may be the North Korean hacker group Lazarus Group.

CoinEx suffered a hot wallet private key compromise on September 12, 2023, allowing the attacker to drain assets across nine blockchains in a single coordinated operation. Loss estimates range from $53 million to $70 million, with attribution to North Korea’s Lazarus Group. CoinEx rebuilt wallet infrastructure and pledged full user reimbursement, but the exact technical cause and chain-level transaction detail remain unverified. A compromise of centralized hot wallet private keys enabled unauthorized withdrawals from CoinEx wallets on multiple chains. The lack of multisig or hardware-bound custody allowed a single leak to expose assets across all supported blockchains.…

On September 12, 2023, the centralized cryptocurrency exchange CoinEx suffered a compromise of its hot wallet keys, resulting in a coordinated theft of approximately $54,$55 million in digital assets across more than nine blockchains. The incident is attributed to North Korea's Lazarus Group. The private keys for CoinEx's hot wallets were compromised, allowing attackers to drain assets across multiple blockchains nearly simultaneously. As the key management system enabled a single private-key compromise to affect all chains, funds were lost before effective action could be taken.

Various blockchain watchers noticed suspicious transfers from a hot wallet known to belong to the CoinEx cryptocurrency exchange. CoinEx later confirmed a "security incident" involving "unauthorized transactions", and disclosed that around $70 million was stolen. Outside researchers have suggested that the thieves appear to be a part of the North Korean state-sponsored hacking group, Lazarus. CoinEx is based out of Hong Kong, and was recently forced to stop serving US customers as part of a settlement with the New York Attorney General which also required them to pay a $1.7 million fine.
